newsitem.title: USA: Texaco realigning along business lines.
newsitem.headline: Texaco realigning along business lines.

text.p: Texaco Inc said Wednesday its corporate organization will be realigned according to business lines effective January 1.
The company said the new structure will consolidate such units as worldwide exploration and production as well as international refining and marketing operations.
Texaco said it also is creating New Business Development units to provide greater focus on global growth opportunities.
In addition, the company said, it is establishing senior-level Leadership Councils to provide strategic direction and coordination in key business areas.
At corporate headquarters, the realignment moves Patrick J. Lynch, 58, currently vice president of Texaco Inc and president of Texaco Europe, to the chief financial officer's post.
William C. Bousquette, 60, the company's current chief financial officer, has elected to retire at the end of 1996, Texaco said.

In addition to responsibility for the comptrollers, investor relations and shareholder services, risk management, tax and finance functions, the office of the CFO will have responsibility for corporate planning and economics, and oil trading and transport, the company said.

It said Allen J. Krowe, 64, will continue as vice chairman of Texaco. Senior Vice President Stephen M. Turner, 57, remains as general counsel, and corporate communications will continue to be led by Senior Vice President William K. Tell, Jr., 62. Corporate Secretary Carl B. Davidson, 63, and President of the Human Resources Division Richard F. Brenner, 56, will remain in their current posts.

Texaco said the realigned operations will be led by a team that combines individuals with long experience in operations with others who bring fresh perspectives to new challenges and responsibilities.

Chief executive Peter I. Bijur said the realignment affects reporting and management functions, not ongoing field operations. While some overlapping activities may be eliminated, the new structure is designed to stimulate growth rather than simply cut costs.

"The petroleum business today is global and intensely competitive. To succeed in this environment, and build on our current performance, we must be able to grow our existing businesses, and identify, analyze and execute on new opportunities more swiftly," Bijur explained.
"That demands that we move faster, communicate better and coordinate more closely" to maximize chosen markets.
"By placing groups which perform similar work in the same location," Bijur added, they will be able to move information throughout the organization more directly and openly."
He emphasized the New Business Development groups as a key new element of Texaco's organization.
He said the Leadership Councils will be the central means of setting strategy, policy and coordinating activities across business lines and throughout the company.
"The Councils will help to make Texaco function as a seamless organization," Bijur said.
